The for-jumps program matches the lesson snippet: continue still runs i++ and break skips it, so i stays 3 (§12.8, §12.7.1). §12.7.2 says the repeat count is evaluated once, and a negative, x or z count runs zero times; that matches the repeat-1101, repeat-x and repeat-change-n lead-in, and the lead-in does not reveal the repeat-change-n answer. §12.7.3 says higher-cardinality indices change faster and the loop iterates from the left bound to the right bound. S2 L151 - The 'Try it' lead-in says 'Notice that only `%0` changes the field width'. That is false. IEEE 1800-2023 §21.2.1.2 says a field width is any non-negative decimal integer constant placed between % and the radix letter, so %5d and %3h are legal and change the width. 0 is only the special case that gives the minimum width. The lesson also contradicts the sentence a few lines later, where real values take C-style width (§21.2.1.1, Table 21-2, '%10.3g specifies a minimum field width of 10'). The PrintingLab assumptions also say explicit widths such as %3d are simply not shown, not that they do not exist. -> Reword it, for example: 'Notice that `%0` shrinks the field to the minimum width, while the plain specifier pads to the width of the largest value the type can hold.'
